title: A normal ring is integrally closed in its total ring of fractions
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative normal ring [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $S$ be the set of nonzerodivisors of $R$ and $Q(R)=S^{-1}R$ its total ring of fractions [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Then every element of $Q(R)$ integral over $R$ lies in the image of the localization map $R\to Q(R)$; equivalently, $R$ is integrally closed in $Q(R)$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 034M (lemma-normal-ring-integrally-closed, line 8218), with its proof

proof.text: Fix an element x = a/s in Q(R), with a in R and s in S [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Since s is a nonzerodivisor, the map R to Q(R) is injective: r/1 = 0 implies ur = 0 for some u in S, hence r = 0. Fix any prime p of R. The image s/1 is nonzero in the domain R_p [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]: if it were zero, some t outside p would satisfy ts = 0 in R, forcing t = 0 in p. Thus (a/1)/(s/1) is defined in the fraction field of R_p. It is integral over R_p, since the monic equation for x maps coefficientwise to one for this fraction.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 034M (lemma-normal-ring-integrally-closed, lines 8223-8229), first half; the nonzerodivisor check spells out the source's flat-localization inclusion

proof.text: By normality [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], R_p is a domain integrally closed in its fraction field, so the fraction from Step 1 is b/f for some b in R and f outside p [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Equality (a/1)/(s/1) = (b/1)/(f/1) in that fraction field gives (fa - bs)/1 = 0 in R_p, since its map into its fraction field is injective. By the localization equality criterion, there is t outside p with t(fa - bs) = 0 in R. In Q(R) this implies (tf)x = tb/1, because s becomes a unit there; and tf is outside p since p is prime. Let I be the set of u in R such that (u/1)x lies in R as a subring of Q(R), an ideal since R embeds in Q(R) by Step 1. Then tf is in I and outside p. Since p was arbitrary, I is contained in no prime ideal.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 034M (lemma-normal-ring-integrally-closed, lines 8227-8237), local membership and denominator clearing

proof.text: If I is not R, then [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal] gives a maximal ideal m containing I; every maximal ideal is prime, contrary to Step 2. Therefore I = R, so 1 is in I and x is in R as a subring of Q(R). This proves every element of Q(R) integral over R comes from R.
